figures.finding: Lithuania's Film Tax Incentive covers up to 30% of a film's production budget through a local company's investment, which the company deducts from its taxable income; at least 80% of eligible costs and no less than €43,000 must be spent in Lithuania, and actors' pay above 4% of production costs is not eligible. The scheme runs in its current form to 31 December 2028.

value.scheme: Lithuanian Film Tax Incentive (Lietuvos kino centras)
value.base: production budget, via private donor investment

figures.applies: Lithuania, domestic, co-produced and service productions through a Lithuanian production company.

sources.said: From 2019 Lithuanian Film Tax Incentive offers an opportunity to save up to 30% of the film production budget through private investment scheme. … The incentive is available for the production of feature films, TV dramas, documentaries and animated films. … At least 80% of eligible film production costs must be incurred in Lithuania and the total amount of eligible spend in Lithuania has to be no less than 43,000 EUR. … Payment for actors (if the payment exceeds 4% of the production costs of the film or its part).

Implemented in 2014, the Lithuanian Film Tax Incentive covers up to 30% of the production budget. The scheme will be effective in its current form until 31 December 2028. Since 2014, 669 productions have benefited from the Lithuanian Film Tax Incentive by getting a total of €133,4 million in investment for film production.

figures.finding: The Lithuanian Film Centre funds the development and production of national films selectively, in two calls a year, from a budget of €7.2 million in 2025 (€6.5 million in 2024).
figures.applies: Lithuania, film producers registered in the EU/EEA with a Lithuanian establishment at payment.

sources.said: NATURE OF FUNDING: Selective CULTURAL TEST: Applies SESSIONS PER YEAR: 2 (spring, autumn). … ANNUAL BUDGET FOR FILM DEVELOPMENT, PRODUCTION AND CO-PRODUCTION 7,2 million EUR in 2025 6,5 million EUR in 2024 5,7 million EUR in 2023 5,5 million EUR in 2022

figures.finding: Lithuanian cinemas sold 3.57 million tickets in 2025 for €23.7 million; the year's top film was the Lithuanian 'The Southern Chronicles' with 412,521 admissions (€3.14 million), and seven of the top ten Lithuanian films drew under 40,000 admissions.
